images.title: Diagonals of a rectangle
images.purpose: Show that the two diagonals of a rectangle PQRS are equal in length.
images.composition: One large rectangle centred with wide white space around it, nothing else.
images.exact_structure: One rectangle PQRS, 6 cm long and 4 cm wide, outline plain, with corners P bottom left, Q bottom right, R top right, S top left. Diagonal PR drawn teal #0072B2 and diagonal QS drawn amber #E69F00, crossing at the centre. Both diagonals drawn to exactly the same length, about 7.2 cm. Exactly 1 rectangle, 2 diagonals.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
two diagonals drawn with visibly different lengths
images.takeaway: The two diagonals of a rectangle are equal.
images.description: A 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle PQRS with diagonal PR in teal and diagonal QS in amber, both the same length.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at each diagonal in turn and say that the two have the same length.

image_decisions.why: Equal diagonals of a rectangle is a single clear picture.
